extracted.intended_audience: academic authors preparing responses to peer reviewer comments (manuscript revision authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on how to draft a structured, professional, and effective rebuttal/response letter and corresponding manuscript revisions after peer review. Covers reading and grouping comments, revision workflow, tone, format, and handling disagreements or conflicting reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors' evaluation priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors evaluate revised manuscripts not only on the changes but also on the quality of revisions, the tone of the response letter, and whether reviewer concerns were genuinely addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poorly handled responses can lead to rejection even after major revisions. Effective responses signal professionalism and editorial maturity; demonstrate that reviewer concerns were genuinely addressed rather than superficially edited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read reviewer comments objectively before responding
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not respond immediately; read all comments carefully and objectively to avoid defensive or rushed replies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before drafting replies: read all comments carefully; group them into major and minor points; identify overlapping concerns. This preparation improves the quality of addressing reviewer comments and prevents defensive or rushed responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the reviewer's underlying concern
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify whether a comment signals confusion, methodological concern, interpretive issue, or scope problem, rather than taking wording at face value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may phrase comments indirectly (e.g., a request to 'clarify' often signals confusion, not minor wording). Ask: Is the concern about clarity, method, interpretation, or scope? Does the comment affect the paper’s core argument? This mindset is central to effective responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise the manuscript before writing the response letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the substantive manuscript revisions first so the rebuttal letter aligns with the revised text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice: make all revisions first; track changes carefully; note page and line numbers. Editors expect the revised manuscript and rebuttal letter to align perfectly; doing revisions first streamlines revision and improves editorial trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to every comment even if you disagree
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge each reviewer point; do not ignore comments even when you decide not to implement suggested changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When disagreeing: be respectful and evidence-based; explain why the change was not made; support your position with references or rationale. Professional rebuttal letter writing values explanation over compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a clear, structured response format
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the response so editors and reviewers can easily follow which comment is being addressed and what was done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A typical format includes: Reviewer comment (quoted or summarized); Author response; Description of revision. This structure shows organization and respect for the peer review process and makes it easier for editors to verify changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a professional and neutral tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep tone courteous, non-defensive, and professional throughout the response letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid emotional or defensive language. Use neutral, appreciative phrasing such as 'We thank the reviewer for this insightful comment…' and 'We have revised the manuscript to clarify…' Tone matters as much as content and reinforces credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific about what you changed
rubrics_metrics.description: State concretely what edits were made, where they appear, and why they improve the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague responses. Always state: What was changed; Where it was changed (page/line/section); Why it improves the manuscript. Specificity is one of the most effective tips and reduces follow-up queries from editors or reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address conflicting reviewer comments strategically
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewers disagree, explain how you balanced competing suggestions and justify your final decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how you balanced the feedback and justify your final decision; inform the editor if necessary. Handling conflicting comments well demonstrates editorial awareness during manuscript revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use expert support for high-stakes or complex revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider external professional assistance when revisions are extensive, complex, or strategically important for acceptance in indexed journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External services can help interpret reviewer intent, strengthen rebuttal logic, and align revisions with journal expectations. This support is especially valuable for early-career researchers or submissions to indexed databases like Scopus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate major and minor comments and allocate effort accordingly
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify comments into major and minor points to prioritize revision effort while addressing all items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group comments into major and minor points and allocate more detailed explanations to major comments. However, both types should be addressed with care; major comments usually require more detailed explanations and potentially larger manuscript changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide appropriate length and completeness for each comment
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no fixed length for responses; each reviewer comment should be addressed clearly and completely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on clarity and completeness rather than length. Some responses will be brief (for minor edits) and others longer (for methodological or interpretive issues). The key is thoroughness: every comment must be acknowledged and answered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track changes and cite exact locations for edits
rubrics_metrics.description: When describing revisions, include page and line numbers or markups to help editors and reviewers verify edits quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tracked changes in the manuscript and reference exact page/line/section locations in the response. This practice streamlines verification and signals precise, transparent revision work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate respect, academic responsibility, and evidence-based justification
rubrics_metrics.description: The overarching goal of responses is to show respect for the review process, academic responsibility, and to justify scholarly decisions with evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explanation and evidence when making choices; show that revisions (or decisions not to revise) are grounded in scholarship. This behavior builds trust with editors and reviewers and supports long-term publication success.
